extraction.name: Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art
extraction.description: A paper that reviews recent progress in remote sensing image scene classification, proposes the publicly available NWPU-RESISC45 benchmark dataset, and evaluates representative state-of-the-art methods on it.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, and Xiaoqiang Lu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was extracted by experts in remote sensing image interpretation from Google Earth imagery, which maps the Earth by superimposing images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data onto a 3D globe. The authors selected representative scene classes by first reviewing existing datasets and then searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar to identify additional scene categories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Remote sensing images from Google Earth; images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and GIS overlays; existing remote sensing scene datasets and literature sources used to identify scene classes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were carefully selected under different weather, season, illumination, imaging conditions, and scales. The dataset was constructed by selecting 45 scene classes and collecting 700 images per class, with images resized to 256×256 pixels in RGB space.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scene images were manually extracted as local image patches from large-scale remote sensing images. The paper does not describe additional preprocessing beyond selection, extraction, and resizing to 256×256 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The paper does not describe a human annotation protocol for labels beyond assigning images to 45 scene classes during dataset construction. For the Brazilian coffee scene dataset reviewed in the paper, identification of coffee crops was performed manually by agricultural researchers, with tiles assigned to classes based on coffee pixel thresholds.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable the community to develop and evaluate data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification, supporting applications such as natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that many existing datasets are biased by small scale, limited scene diversity, and saturation of accuracy. The proposed dataset is designed to reduce these issues by including rich variations, high within-class diversity, and between-class similarity.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper does not state formal limitations of the proposed dataset beyond noting that some classes such as island, lake, mountain, and snowberg have lower spatial resolutions. It also notes that the dataset is challenging due to high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, training, testing, and evaluation of remote sensing image scene classification methods, including handcrafted features, unsupervised feature learning methods, and deep learning-based CNN methods.
